Advancing the World’s Technology Together

Our technology solutions power the tools you use every day--including smartphones, electric vehicles, hyperscale data centers, IoT devices, and so much more. Here, you’ll have an opportunity to be part of a global leader whose innovative designs are pushing the boundaries of what’s possible and powering the future.

We believe innovation and growth are driven by an inclusive culture and a diverse workforce. We’re dedicated to empowering people to be their true selves. Together, we’re building a better tomorrow for our employees, customers, partners, and communities.

What You’ll Learn

- Project Overview: In memory-centric AI accelerators, many memory devices each process data in place and only exchange small partial results, which are then merged. As LLM attention evolves from grouped-query attention (GQA) to multi-head latent attention (MLA) and sparse top-k attention, the work done locally on each device shrinks while cross-device merge and reduction increasingly dominate decode latency. Using the team’s in-house performance model and simulator, you will explore the design space of merge/reduction architectures — where reduction happens, how devices are connected, and at what precision partial results are exchanged — and propose an architecture that performs well across modern attention workloads.

- Skills You’ll Learn:

- Architecture-level performance modeling and design-space exploration for distributed, memory-centric AI accelerators

- How modern attention variants (GQA, MLA, sparse top-k attention) map onto distributed memory, and how they shift the balance between computation and communication

- Hardware–software co-design of interconnect and reduction (collective) hardware for LLM inference

What You’ll Do

The AGI team at Samsung Semiconductor explores memory-centric system architectures for next-generation AI inference, where computation happens close to where data lives. We co-design hardware and software to make large-scale LLM inference faster and more efficient, and our work informs Samsung’s future memory and accelerator products. As an intern, you will own a research-driven architecture study end to end — from workload modeling to design-space exploration and an architecture proposal — working closely with architects and performance-modeling engineers, and you will present your findings to the broader organization at the end of the summer.

Location: Daily onsite presence at our San Jose headquarters in alignment with our Flexible Work polic

Reports to: Director

- Extend the team’s in-house performance model and simulator to capture modern attention workloads — GQA, MLA, and sparse top-k attention — during LLM decode.

- Analyze how each attention variant changes the balance between local computation and cross-device merge/reduction traffic, and pinpoint when merge becomes the bottleneck.

- Explore the merge/reduction design space, including where reduction happens (centralized, in-network, or hierarchical), interconnect topology, link bandwidth and latency, and partial-result precision.

- Characterize token-selection patterns of sparse attention models and design distributed top-k selection and data-placement strategies that minimize communication and load imbalance.

- Estimate first-order area and power costs of proposed reduction hardware and weigh them against performance gains.

- Validate the numerical accuracy of reduced-precision merging against full-precision reference implementations.

- Collaborate weekly with your mentor and architecture engineers, and share your results through team meetings, a final presentation, and a technical report that inform future accelerator architecture and potential publications or patents.

- Complete other responsibilities as assigned.

What You Bring

- Pursuing a Master’s or PhD in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field preferred.

- Must have at least 1 academic quarter/semester remaining

- Strong background in computer architecture, including memory systems, interconnects/networks-on-chip, and performance analysis.

- Solid understanding of Transformer inference, including attention variants (MHA/GQA/MLA), the KV cache, and the decode phase.

- Proficiency in Python and/or C++, with hands-on experience using or building architecture simulators or analytical performance models.

- Preferred: familiarity with sparse attention (e.g., DeepSeek Sparse Attention, NSA, Quest), online-softmax merging as in FlashAttention/FlashDecoding, or in-network reduction; publications in venues such as ISCA, MICRO, HPCA, ASPLOS, or MLSys.

- You’re inclusive, adapting your style to the situation and diverse global norms of our people.

- An avid learner, you approach challenges with curiosity and resilience, seeking data to help build understanding.

- You’re collaborative, building relationships, humbly offering support and openly welcoming approaches.

- Innovative and creative, you proactively explore new ideas and adapt quickly to change.

Project Overview
The Global E-commerce ecosystem has accumulated massive heterogeneous data, including user behavior, product images and text, multimedia content, sales data, and logistics time series. However, traditional models still face significant limitations in long-term forecasting, cross-modal understanding, and complex decision-making.
This project aims to build a foundational large model tailored for Global E-commerce scenarios. It will unify key elements such as users, products, content, logistics, and inventory into a single modeling framework. On top of this, a modular, pluggable Agent framework will be designed to integrate capabilities such as task planning, tool usage, multi-turn interaction, and environmental awareness. Please include “accommodation request” in the subject line title and be sure to include your name, the job ID, and your preferred method of contact in the body of the email. Emails not related to accommodation requests will not receive responses. Applicants may also call 877-968-7762 and say "Workday" for accommodation assistance. All information provided will be kept confidential and will be used only to the extent required to provide needed reasonable accommodations.

At PNC we foster an inclusive and accessible workplace. We provide reasonable accommodations to employment applicants and qualified individuals with a disability who need an accommodation to perform the essential functions of their positions.
